lines.text: The gates stay open, of course.
The gates close, Pak. The roads close. The airport closes.
What is the cost of one day of zero revenue?
Zero. Nobody on the island is spending either.
...I hate that this makes sense.

14.label: PANEL 5 · SYSTEM
14.text: A blue window over the base.

lines.text: [QUEST: OPERATION SILENCE] [37 RENTERS · 37 BIKES · 100% BY TOMORROW NIGHT]

14.label: PANEL 6 · PRODUCT, COMEDY (Bees Pro beat)
14.text: Outside the base. Komang loads the crew's Nyepi supplies onto a red Bees Pro: two blue water gallons stand on the flat footboard, rice and snacks in a box on the seat behind him. He tries to balance a THIRD gallon on his knees.

lines.text: Two fit on the floor. The third one is... emotional support.
[OVERWEIGHT? NO. OVERCONFIDENT.]
Two gallons. Two trips. You have three days.

14.label: PANEL 7 · MONTAGE, PRODUCT
14.text: The crew delivering across the island: Arya on his olive Athena at a villa gate in Ubud, Sekar on her pink Athena in Seminyak, Dewa on his grey EdPower in Uluwatu. On each bike's display, the battery reads full.

lines.text: The day before the silence, every Werigo bike goes home full.

14.label: PANEL 8
14.text: A tourist family at a villa gate, confused, holding a printed notice.

lines.text: So we can't go out at all?
Not for one day. Stay in, keep the lights low, and look up at night.
Look up at what?
You'll see.

14.label: PANEL 9 · SPLASH
14.text: A beach at morning. A long procession in white: women carrying offerings on their heads, men carrying temple umbrellas and sacred objects wrapped in cloth, walking into the sea breeze. Gamelan.

lines.text: Melasti. Before the new year, the island walks its sacred things to the sea to be cleaned.

14.label: PANEL 10
14.text: The grandmother, the Gatekeeper, in white, sprinkling holy water on Arya's and Denisa's heads with a frangipani flower.

lines.text: The sea takes the dirt of the year. Then the island can start again.
Does it take bad habits too?
Only if you let go of them.

14.label: PANEL 11 · VFX
14.text: As the water touches Arya, his System window flickers and a thin line of static runs through it.

lines.text: [SIGNAL WEAKENING] [...]
The System... is shaking?

14.label: PANEL 12
14.text: The airport, the evening before Nyepi. The arrivals board, most rows already showing CLOSED. Through the doors come CHLOE (messy blonde bun, sunglasses on her head) and JAKE (sandy surfer hair, Hawaiian shirt, surfboard bag).

lines.text: We made it! The last flight before the island turns off!
The pilot said "enjoy the silence". I thought it was a joke.

14.label: PANEL 13 · PRODUCT
14.text: Outside, Arya is waiting beside a YELLOW Wedison Athena, a navy EdPower behind it with a surf rack.

lines.text: You said save the yellow one.
You SAVED it?!
It has been waiting since your postcard. Charged to one hundred.

14.label: PANEL 14 · VFX
14.text: A gold window opens over Chloe, the same one from CH.5, now with a new line.

lines.text: [VISITOR PASS · RENEWED] [RETURNING PLAYER BONUS: +1 FRIEND]
What's the friend bonus?
Komang is cooking tonight.

14.label: PANEL 15
14.text: Dusk at a crossroads. Offerings (tawur) on the ground, a priest sprinkling holy water, men beating kulkul drums, children banging pots.

lines.text: The night before the silence is the loudest night of the year.

14.label: PANEL 16 · SPLASH, VFX
14.text: The ogoh-ogoh parade. Torches, drums, and Putu's giant ogoh-ogoh on a bamboo platform carried by twenty young men. Its face is a scowling demon with fangs and... thick black rectangular glasses.

lines.text: I call him BHUTA DEADLINE.
Why does he look like Pak Chan?
I don't know what you mean.

14.label: PANEL 17 · VFX, FANTASY
14.text: The ogoh-ogoh's eyes glow red. For a second it seems to turn its head toward the crowd. Shadow-spirits swirl around the torches.

lines.text: SYSTEM (red, glitching): [BHUTA KALA DETECTED] [LEVEL: ANNUAL]

14.label: PANEL 18
14.text: The young men spin the ogoh-ogoh three times at the crossroads, shouting, so the demons get confused and lose their way.

lines.text: Make noise, scare them, spin them. Then tomorrow we go quiet, and they think Bali is empty. And they leave.
So the whole island pretends nobody's home?
For one day. It works every year.

14.label: PANEL 19 · COMEDY, SPLIT
14.text: Meanwhile in Hong Kong, the same week: under the Canal Road flyover, an old woman beats a paper figure with a slipper. Pak Liam (the owner, white golf polo) stands beside Pak Chan and Pak Remy, who look very uncomfortable.

lines.text: Hong Kong. The same week. Jingzhe, the Awakening of Insects.
Villain hitting. You write the name of your trouble, she beats it away.
(writing on the paper) "Late payments."

14.label: PANEL 20 · COMEDY
14.text: The old woman hits the paper with her slipper, very fast. Pak Chan hands her a second paper.

lines.text: And you, Chan?
(quietly) ...Stress.
That one costs extra.
Two islands. The same idea. Chase away what haunts you, then start again.

14.label: PANEL 22 · SPLASH
14.text: 06:00. The island is empty. A long empty road past a temple gate, a closed warung with its shutters down. No bikes, no cars, only birds on the power lines. Morning mist.

lines.text: [NYEPI · 06:00] [AMATI GENI · AMATI KARYA · AMATI LELUNGAN · AMATI LELANGUAN]
No fire. No work. No travel. No entertainment.

14.label: PANEL 23 · VFX
14.text: Arya wakes up at home. His System window tries to open and fails, breaking into static, then vanishes.

lines.text: [SYSTEM OFFLINE]
...Hello?
(Nothing answers.)

14.label: PANEL 24
14.text: Arya sits on the step of his family compound, no phone, no quest. His mother sweeps nothing, quietly, then sits beside him.

lines.text: No quests today?
No anything today.
Good. You were a person before you were a player.

14.label: PANEL 25 · COMEDY
14.text: Komang tiptoes along the empty lane carrying a bag of snacks, sneaking to Arya's house. A torchlight hits him. PAK GEDE, the pecalang, stands in the middle of the road.

lines.text: Where are you going?
...Nowhere. I'm meditating. While walking.
Meditate at home.

14.label: PANEL 26 · SYSTEM, COMEDY
14.text: A tiny grey window glitches over Pak Gede.

lines.text: SYSTEM (grey, flickering): [PAK GEDE · CLASS: WARDEN · RANK: UNDEFEATED]
(walking back home) Even the System is scared of him.

14.label: PANEL 27
14.text: Chloe and Jake at their villa, sitting on the floor playing cards in daylight, whispering.

lines.text: Why are we whispering? Nobody can hear us.
The whole island is whispering. It feels rude not to.

14.label: PANEL 28
14.text: Denisa at her villa writes in a paper notebook with a pencil, her laptop closed beside her. Her neighbour's offering at the gate. The white Victory parked, silent.

lines.text: Thirty countries. This is the first one that asked me to stop.

14.label: PANEL 29
14.text: ODY at his rented house, sitting on the floor with his back against the wall. His phone on the floor beside him shows NO SERVICE.

lines.text: SYSTEM (grey, fading): [ODY · ACTIVE QUESTS: 14 → 0]

14.label: PANEL 30 · FLASHBACK
14.text: Small panels: Singapore, the fast parallel meetings from CH.12, three calls at once, the gold and bronze tier windows, the midnight messages.

lines.text: Since Singapore I've never stopped. Not one day.

14.label: PANEL 31
14.text: His Balinese neighbour, an old man, leans over the low wall and quietly passes ODY a banana leaf with rice and a little sambal. Not a word.

lines.text: (whispering) Suksma, Pak.
(whispering) Eat. Then sit. That's the whole job today.

14.label: PANEL 32 · EMOTIONAL
14.text: ODY eats slowly on the step. Behind him, his Athena is parked in the shade, silent as always.

lines.text: The island is quiet one day a year. The bikes are quiet every day. Maybe that's why it worked here.

14.label: PANEL 33 · COMEDY
14.text: Singapore, the same morning, 09:00. Pak Chan at his desk. On his phone, a chat with ODY. One grey tick on every message.

lines.text: ODY.
ODY?
The numbers.

14.label: PANEL 34 · COMEDY
14.text: Pak Remy at the door.

lines.text: Pak, the whole of Bali is offline. Even the internet.
The whole island?
The whole island.
...Then who am I shouting at?

14.label: PANEL 35 · COMEDY
14.text: Pak Chan tries silence: he puts the phone face down, crosses his arms, closes his eyes. A small timer window counts.

lines.text: [SILENCE ATTEMPT · 00:11] [FAILED]
(He checks the phone. Still one grey tick.)

14.label: PANEL 36
14.text: Evening in Singapore. The office is empty. Pak Chan alone at the window, the city lights bright below. He closes his laptop slowly. On the desk, the paper figure from Hong Kong, a slipper print on the word STRESS.

lines.text: ...Quiet.
SYSTEM (grey, very faint): [EVEN THE BOARD IS QUIET]

14.label: PANEL 37 · SPLASH, VFX
14.text: Night over Bali. No lights anywhere, only the Milky Way, huge and bright, over the rice fields, the temples and the dark sea.

lines.text: With every light off, the island can finally see the sky.

14.label: PANEL 38 · VFX
14.text: Small panels, all looking up: Arya with his mother on the compound step; Komang lying on his roof; Chloe and Jake on a villa lawn; Denisa at her gate; Sekar and Dewa each in their own garden; ODY on his step.

lines.text: (whispering) ...Oh.
(whispering) That's what she meant. Look up.

14.label: PANEL 39 · VFX, FANTASY
14.text: The stars move. Slowly they form constellations of each player's class sign: a delivery box for Arya, a compass for Komang, a wave for Jake, a small house for Denisa, a key for ODY.

lines.text: SYSTEM (gold, very faint, written in starlight): [...REBOOTING]

14.label: PANEL 40 · VFX
14.text: The grandmother at her gate with a tiny oil lamp hidden under her shawl. Behind her, faint glowing lines run under the whole island like roots: niskala, the unseen side.

lines.text: The island rests one day so it can carry all of us for the rest of the year.

14.label: PANEL 41 · COMEDY
14.text: 06:00 the next morning. Phones come back to life all over the island at once. ODY's phone vibrates off the step.

lines.text: BZZT BZZT BZZT BZZT
[SIGNAL RESTORED] [UNREAD: 412]

14.label: PANEL 42 · COMEDY
14.text: ODY reads Pak Chan's chat: a long column of "ODY?" and, at the very bottom, one message sent at midnight.

lines.text: ...Was it quiet?
Very.
Good. Now sell.

14.label: PANEL 43
14.text: Ngembak Geni. Families visit each other, shake hands and ask forgiveness. Arya shakes Komang's hand formally.

lines.text: Forgive me for everything this year.
Forgive me for the snacks I ate from your bag during Nyepi.
...What snacks?

14.label: PANEL 44 · PRODUCT, SPLASH
14.text: Morning. Chloe on the yellow Athena and Jake on the navy EdPower, surfboard on the side rack, ride out onto a fresh empty road with Denisa on her white Victory, open-face helmets on, grinning. Every bike full, silent, no queue.

lines.text: The bikes slept too. Every Werigo bike woke up full.
[QUEST COMPLETE: OPERATION SILENCE] [RENTERS WHO EXTENDED: 7 · COMPLAINTS: 0]

14.label: PANEL 45
14.text: Pak Remy's appraisal window on a video call.

lines.text: Revenue on Nyepi: zero. Complaints: zero. Extensions: seven.
Quiet sells.
...I'm writing that down.

14.label: PANEL 46 · VFX
14.text: Arya's System window finally opens again, clean and bright, with a new line.

lines.text: [SYSTEM ONLINE] [NEW PASSIVE SKILL: STILLNESS · RECOVER FULLY AFTER ONE DAY OF SILENCE]
It came back.
It never left. You just finally heard it.

14.label: PANEL 47
14.text: Video call. Pak Chan, rested, sharper than ever.

lines.text: Next week I'm in Bali. Jimbaran to Tanjung Benoa. We are finding the building.
Which building, Pak?
The Citadel.

14.label: PANEL 48 · SPLASH, VFX
14.text: Dewa on his grey EdPower at the front of a line of Wedison bikes on the Jimbaran coast road, sunset behind, a huge faint outline of a glass building in the sky.

lines.text: [WORLD EVENT INCOMING: THE CITADEL]

14.label: Closing
14.text: To be continued... NEXT CHAPTER: CH.15 · THE CITADEL. What would you do with one day of total silence? Tell us in the comments.

15.text: Pak Chan and Pak Remy arrive in Bali.

lines.text: Your ride, Pak. Delivered to the airport, charged and ready.
I don't ride.
I do.

lines.text: Remy takes the helmet. Chan chooses the car.
PAK REMY. NEW SKILL: RIDER

CONVOY LEADER: DEWA. RANK A

15.text: The riders wait under a tree.

lines.text: The Board wants the building by Friday.
Buildings don't care about Friday.

15.text: Pak Chan checks his compass from inside the car.

lines.text: Water in front. A mountain behind. No T-junction at the door. No number four.
That's quite a list, Pak.
Then we had better start.

lines.text: CANDIDATE 1: REJECTED. TIME: 2 SECONDS

15.text: The team inspects prospective buildings.

It contains a four.

lines.text: REJECTED: 3. TIMES CHAN LEFT THE CAR: 0
Six hundred square metres. Price per metre...
Too expensive for a building I haven't left my car for.

15.label: PANEL 11
15.text: The riders wait under a tree.

lines.text: He's looking for the right building from inside a box.
Then he'll never find it.

15.label: PANEL 12
15.text: Pak Chan remains stuck in traffic.

lines.text: HOOONK
TRAFFIC. BOSS LEVEL

15.label: PANEL 13
15.text: Pak Chan remains stuck in traffic.

lines.text: Twelve minutes. Same view.

15.label: PANEL 14
15.text: Dewa offers Pak Chan a helmet and a seat on the EdPower.

lines.text: Is it... comfortable? For two.
It's an EdPower, Pak. It's comfortable for two.

15.label: PANEL 15
15.text: Dewa takes Pak Chan on his first EdPower ride.

lines.text: FIRST RIDE. THE CHAIRMAN FEELS THE WIND

15.label: Pause page
15.text: No engine roar. Just the wind.

15.label: PANEL 16
15.text: The EdPower charges through its centre-tunnel hatch ahead of the closed seat.

lines.text: Ten to eighty percent in about fifteen minutes. One coffee.
I have never waited fifteen minutes for anything.
You waited twelve in the car. For nothing.

15.label: PANEL 17
15.text: The group stops for coffee while charging.

lines.text: How many of them have never had a chance to try these bikes?
That's why we need the Citadel. Let them ride. Then decide.

15.label: PANEL 18
15.text: Cinta finds a promising plot of land.

lines.text: My ground sense says this one. Water in front. Room to breathe.

15.label: PANEL 19
15.text: Cinta introduces Jero Undagi.

lines.text: This is Jero Undagi. He knows this land better than any of us.

15.label: PANEL 20
15.text: Jero Undagi and Pak Remy measure the land.

lines.text: Forty point two metres.
Twenty-three depa and a musti.
...Is that a lot?

15.label: PANEL 21
15.text: Jero Undagi and Pak Remy measure the land.

lines.text: We measure with the body of the person who will use it. A house should fit its owner.
Who are you building this for?
Everyone who has never ridden one yet.

15.label: PANEL 22
15.text: The System reveals a blueprint.

lines.text: ASTA KOSALA KOSALI. MEASUREMENT ACCEPTED

15.label: Pause page
15.text: A place should fit the people who use it.

15.label: PANEL 23
15.text: Pak Chan and Jero Undagi discuss two traditions.

lines.text: TWO TRADITIONS. ONE CONVERSATION
Water in front. Good fortune.
Here, kaja points toward the mountain, our sacred direction. We must read this land on its own terms.
Then show me.

15.label: PANEL 24
15.text: The atmosphere on the land changes.

lines.text: Then the wind changed.

15.label: PANEL 25
15.text: Pak Remy notices an unsettling reflection.

lines.text: UNKNOWN ENTITY: ???. LAND OWNER: NOT YOU
...Pak Chan. The numbers are all fours.

15.label: PANEL 26
15.text: The guardian of the land appears.

lines.text: We are leaving.
Sit down. It's the penunggu. The guardian of this land.

15.label: PANEL 27
15.text: The guardian of the land appears.

lines.text: You asked the seller. There is someone else to greet.
Who?
The one who was here before the seller's grandfather.

15.label: PANEL 28
15.text: Jero Undagi explains respect for the land through a traditional painting.

lines.text: Before we build, we ask permission. We make offerings and restore balance with the land.

15.label: PANEL 29
15.text: Pak Chan and Jero Undagi speak about incense and auspicious days.

lines.text: In Hong Kong, my family also burns incense and chooses a good day before building.
Then you know how to begin. By listening.

15.label: PANEL 30
15.text: The group returns after preparations for the ceremony.

lines.text: After the preparations, they return for the ceremony.

15.label: PANEL 31
15.text: The group returns after preparations for the ceremony.

lines.text: What is the ROI of a ceremony?
A building that stands.
...I'll put it under infrastructure.

15.label: PANEL 32
15.text: The guardian acknowledges the group.

lines.text: THE GUARDIAN NODS. PERMISSION GRANTED

15.label: Pause page
15.text: The land has been heard.

15.label: PANEL 33
15.text: A flower falls as Grandmother speaks with Pak Chan.

lines.text: It likes you.
...Good.

15.label: PANEL 34
15.text: The proposed Experience Centre takes shape in their imagination.

lines.text: CITADEL BLUEPRINT: 80%. PROPOSED EXPERIENCE CENTRE
See every bike. Touch it. Try it. Charge while you eat. Rent from Werigo if you're not ready to buy.

15.label: PANEL 35
15.text: The proposed Experience Centre takes shape in their imagination.

lines.text: And the corner with the question mark?
That's for later.

15.label: PANEL 36
15.text: They discuss the right day to begin.

lines.text: What price are you suggesting?
What day is good?
Not this month.
...Of course.

15.label: PANEL 37
15.text: Dewa and Pak Chan ride back together.

lines.text: PAK CHAN: RIDES TAKEN 2. COMPLAINTS: 0

15.label: PANEL 38
15.text: Dewa and Pak Chan ride back together.

lines.text: Dewa.
Pak?
Tomorrow I will ride in front.
...On your own bike?
I didn't say that.

15.label: PANEL 39
15.text: Arya arranges Pak Remy’s rental.

lines.text: NEW ROLE. THE BOARD BECOMES THE CUSTOMER
Keep it for the three days. We'll collect it at the airport.
How much?
It's on the Werigo WhatsApp, Pak. Like everyone else.

15.label: PANEL 40
15.text: Pak Chan and Ody discuss Werigo’s place in the Citadel.

lines.text: The Citadel will be Wedison's. The showroom team will run it.
And Werigo?
Werigo will have a desk. In the corner.

15.label: PANEL 41
15.text: Ody considers the desk offered to Werigo.

lines.text: A desk isn't a home, Pak. The showroom crew already sell bikes all day.
Werigo needs its own shop. Its own crew. Its own fleet.

15.label: Pause page
15.text: Its own shop. Its own crew. Its own fleet.

15.text: The System issues a new main quest.

Then prove Werigo can stand alone.

lines.text: RETURN REQUEST|NO ACTIVE RENTAL

16.label: PANEL 3
16.text: That morning. One bike. Two promises.

lines.text: This key is allocated to tomorrow’s guest.
Then why is it on the showroom test-ride list?
Two calendars. Nobody owns the handover.
The team is doing two jobs. Both need their full attention.
One supervised trial. A separate rental allocation. Your own crew.
Show us who is responsible when the plan changes.
And a place that is ours.
Earn it. Without doing every job yourself.

You make that sound very simple.
It should be. For the guest.

Tell us while we can still fix it.

16.label: PANEL 9
16.text: Bram Ardan. Hospitality beverage sales. Old friend.

lines.text: You look like a spreadsheet learned to suffer.
Good morning to you too, Bram.
Still hiring people who can survive you?
You survived your first sales visit.
I came to sell bottles. I left with a friend and cold sushi.

16.label: PANEL 11
16.text: 2025. Ody’s sushi restaurant and bar.

lines.text: Ten minutes. Let me show you the range.
Ten. The kitchen is still open.

16.label: PANEL 12
16.text: The pitch became a friendship. At parties, they were usually the last two still up. That night, a hired car took them home.

lines.text: You said ten minutes.
You said the last story. Three stories ago.

16.label: PANEL 13
16.text: Present day. A saved message from Selin, Jakarta.

lines.text: SELIN|I miss us. I cannot keep living between visits.
You do not have to explain it today.
Then ask me about the shop.
Fine. Have you eaten?

16.label: PANEL 15
16.text: A few Sundays earlier. After church. No targets. Just people who noticed when Ody went quiet.

16.label: PANEL 16
16.text: He believed meeting Pak Chan and Remy, and building Werigo, was part of that path. It did not mean walking it alone.

lines.text: God, thank You for the people You put beside me. Help me trust them.
A restaurant contact has an empty unit. Easy access. Room for handovers.
We check the access, permission and power before we promise anything.

16.label: PANEL 18
16.text: A trial space. Small enough to run properly.

lines.text: You used to worry about empty tables.
Now I worry about missing helmets. Progress.
Ask the owner. Greet the neighbours. Leave the little shrine its space.
And this old key?
Find out which door it belongs to.
In Singapore, I would choose an auspicious opening time.
Will that move the guest’s flight?

Bike assigned. Battery checked. Both helmets clean.
And the right address?

HANDOVER CHECK|80%+ BATTERY · 2 HELMETS · PHONE HOLDER · BRIEFING

16.label: PANEL 23
16.text: The EdPower’s SuperCharge port sits ahead of the closed seat, on the centre tunnel.

lines.text: Ten to eighty percent in fifteen minutes. Enough time to check the next handover.
One charging slot. One updated delivery time.
If a guest changes hotels, who updates the rider?
Me, after you confirm it.
Good. They should not have to tell three people.
Tomorrow, you make the call. I am here if you need me.
That is somehow reassuring and terrifying.

16.text: 19:47. Three knocks. We are back at the door.

lines.text: RETURN REQUEST|GUEST NAME: UNASSIGNED

16.label: PANEL 27
16.text: Ody lowers his phone. The reflection does not.

It has fewer responsibilities.
Open up. Your dinner is getting cold.
I knew it. Food delivery. Very normal.

16.text: Behind them, the brass key turns once on its hook.

lines.text: Did you put a key through the door?
No. Both hands were full.

Send me the number. I will...
Already done. Arya has the address. Dewa checked the route.

Let us finish it.

16.text: For once, Ody puts his phone face down before it stops ringing. The task stays with its owner.

We did. Each person knew their part.

The helmet-cleaning stool.

16.text: A message from his church group: We saved you a seat for Sunday.

lines.text: Thanks for showing up.
